result.title: SL-Ground: Sentence-Level Grounding for Fine-Grained Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
result.summary: Grounding-based open-vocabulary detectors provide a widely used framework for text-conditioned localization, with a phrase-grounding formulation that aligns object queries to individual text tokens and recovers class scores through token-to-class aggregation. We observe that this token-level scoring design becomes a bottleneck for fine-grained open-vocabulary object detection, where the target category is defined by a complete compositional description rather than by isolated tokens. Based on this observation, we propose SL-Ground, a sentence-level grounding reformulation for grounding-based open-vocabulary detection. Instead of scoring queries against fragmented token evidence, SL-Ground encodes each category description as a complete sentence-level representation and directly scores object queries against these representations. To evaluate fine-grained recognition across label granularity, we construct a multi-granularity Stanford Cars benchmark spanning vehicle type, brand, and car model. At the finest car-model granularity, SL-Ground raises AP over the token-level variant from 14.5 to 70.6 under matched training candidate sampling and to 86.0 with full-vocabulary training, while better preserving open-vocabulary capability and avoiding repeated prompt chunking. Beyond Stanford Cars, SL-Ground also improves FG-OVD performance, achieving the best average AP among compared methods. These results show that sentence-level grounding provides a more suitable scoring unit for fine-grained OVOD and offers a practical path toward fine-grained grounding-based open-vocabulary detectors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SL-Ground，把基于 grounding 的开词汇目标检测从「token 级打分 + token 到类别聚合」改为「句级类别描述表示直接与 object query 对齐打分」，并构建车辆类型／品牌／车型多层级的 Stanford Cars 基准检验细粒度识别效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 用完整句级表示替代碎片化 token 证据的做法，可能为 LVR 中组合式任务描述与视觉证据如何作为整体保留在内部状态、避免信息碎片化提供可核查的方法线索，但其不涉及推理状态生成与更新，迁移需另行设计。
